title: AI Sprint Intelligence Dashboard
description: Pick a synthetic sprint, watch the dashboard fill with team and individual KPIs, get a streaming AI authored meeting brief with workload rebalancing recommendations.

resumeBullet.text: Built an AI Sprint Intelligence Dashboard on Next.js + Vercel. Six monthly sprints across the first half of 2026 with 138 hand curated tickets. Filter by assignee, ticket type, or status to scope the entire dashboard: KPI strip, story points strip, status mix, ETA discipline tiles, per ticket cycle time and aging bars, workload by assignee, sprint health cards, per engineer deep dive with an activity heatmap. A streaming AI meeting brief closes the page. Shares the streaming primitive plus design system with the rest of the portfolio.

portfolioCard.problem: Sprint review prep is one of the most expensive recurring meetings on an engineering team. The lead spends an hour every two weeks consolidating Jira, calling out blockers, and writing a one page summary the room can actually read. Standard Jira dashboards show the data but stop one step short of telling the story.
portfolioCard.approach: Pick a monthly sprint from a six sprint roster (four completed, one in flight at day 17 of 31, one already filling up with backlog tickets a manager has earmarked for next cycle). Filter by assignee, ticket type, or status. The same filter scope feeds every surface on the page: a wide KPI strip plus a story points strip, time in status plus a priority breakdown, ETA discipline tiles (Missing ETA, Overdue), per ticket cycle time and aging bars, workload by assignee, the standard sprint health cards (burndown, velocity, scope creep, carryover), and a per engineer deep dive with an activity heatmap that shows which days each engineer worked on which ticket. A streaming AI meeting brief closes the page with the recommendations that go into the room. Same streaming primitive as Project 1 and Project 2, applied to engineering analytics.
portfolioCard.impact: Sprint review prep drops from an hour per cycle to a five minute read of the AI brief. The dashboard surfaces the right KPIs for the conversation and the activity heatmap shows real per engineer cadence (sequential per week scheduling with hash deterministic profile variation by role, not five tickets running in parallel from day 1). Three engineering moments in the case study: the monorepo rootDirectory workaround for the Vercel deploy, the search param driven filter pattern that feeds every dashboard surface, and the manifest enrichment pattern that keeps cross sprint widgets at zero First Load JS cost.
